verdict.headline: Solid mono-white Soldier go-wide engine, held back by thin card flow, thin ramp and a weak Darien damage half
verdict.summary: The token core works. Makers like Hero of Bladehold, Captain of the Watch, Mobilization and Elspeth, Sun's Champion feed Anointed Procession and Myrel, and the payoffs (Elesh Norn, Field Marshal, Coat of Arms, True Conviction) turn the wide board lethal in one or two attacks. Most of the sweepers spare the Soldiers, and the protection covers Darien and the board. The problems are structural. Draw is 6 against an 11-13 target, tagged ramp is 3 against 9-11, and there are no tutors, so the single-copy engines are hard to find. Darien's self-damage side relies on few real sources. Spot removal is 6 against an 11-13 target, with no real answer to a resolved enchantment or artifact. 22 orphan cards and a synergy density of 0.2333 dilute the concept. Wrath of God and Austere Command also cut against the board. The floor is bracket 3, set solely by Smothering Tithe.

deck_identity.what_it_does: No owner intent is recorded, so this is read from the list. It is a mono-white Soldier token deck. Kjeldoran Outpost, Mobilization, Captain of the Watch, Hero of Bladehold, Myrel, Shield of Argive and the two Elspeths make bodies, and Anointed Procession doubles them. Anthems and lords (Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite, Field Marshal, Glorious Anthem, Marshal's Anthem, Coat of Arms) turn the wide board into lethal attacks. Darien, King of Kjeldor adds a self-damage angle, since damage dealt to you becomes Soldiers. Blood of the Martyr, Jade Monolith and painful lands back it up.
win_paths: Wide Soldier combat: tokens plus anthems and lords attack together. Hero of Bladehold's battle cry, Myrel's token doubling, Odric's forced blocks and True Conviction's double strike and lifelink close the game.
Darien damage engine: self-damage or redirected damage becomes that many Soldiers (doubled by Anointed Procession), feeding the wide board.
Halo Fountain alternate win by untapping fifteen creatures, which the token count makes plausible. It is slow, and so is the incremental reach.
Incremental reach and removal from the token count: Catapult Master exiling creatures by tapping five Soldiers, Dingus Staff pings, and Suture Priest drain.
success_criteria: Soldier production starts early and keeps going. The cheap makers (Precinct Captain, Kjeldoran Outpost, Mobilization, Martial Coup, Elspeth Tirel) and the 4-6 mana makers (Hero of Bladehold, Knight-Captain of Eos, Captain of the Watch) give a wide board by mid-game.

Darien's trigger does real work most games. Enough self-damage sources (Tarnished Citadel, City of Brass, Nomad Stadium, Grand Coliseum, Blood of the Martyr, Jade Monolith) are needed so Soldiers do not depend on opponents attacking.

Enough Soldier payoffs (Captain of the Watch, Field Marshal, Heidegger, Shinra Executive, Myrel, Shield of Argive, Catapult Master) and generic anthems that a typical token board is lethal within a couple of attack steps.

The wipes reset the table without killing the plan. Hour of Reckoning, Mass Calcify, Martial Coup and Elspeth, Sun's Champion leave white tokens alive. Wrath of God and Austere Command should be checked against that.
The deck refuels after a wipe or while building. Skullclamp, Mentor of the Meek, Dawn of a New Age, Haliya, Guided by Light, Halo Fountain and Smothering Tithe keep cards flowing.
Darien and the key engines survive. Bastion Protector, Swiftfoot Boots, Flawless Maneuver and Boromir, Warden of the Tower cover the commander and the board against removal and sweepers.
intentional_quirks: Painful lands and damage redirection in a mono-white deck, where they add no colors.
All basics are Snow-Covered Plains, alongside snow utility lands.
Very high land count with many utility lands and mana sinks, and little traditional ramp.
Heavy lifegain-trigger package of small creatures that do little else.
Several sweepers in a creature deck, most of them token-friendly.

scorecard.one_line: Token makers, Anointed Procession and Myrel form a real engine (synergy.clusters.tokens.support = 14.0), but Darien's damage half runs on thin redirection and Wrath of God/Austere Command cut against the board.
38 lands matches the 38 target (mana.lands) and W sources sit at 35 of 36 recommended, but draw is 6 against a 11-13 target and the six-plus-mana top end has little ramp beyond lands.

Seven sweepers (roles.wipes.count) and five protection pieces cover resets and Darien well, but spot removal sits at 6 against an 11-13 target and the deck has no real answer to a resolved enchantment or artifact.

Wide-combat plan has many redundant carriers (Hero of Bladehold, Myrel, Elesh Norn, True Conviction) and combos.counts.complete = 0 is fine for a go-wide deck, but a single sweeper hurts and there are no tutors (roles.tutors.count = 0).
Floor is bracket 3 solely from Smothering Tithe (bracket.minimum_bracket = 3) with no combos or tutors; the target is unstated, so fit cannot be judged beyond that.

No cap is set and inventory is unavailable, so only cost-efficiency can be judged; Anointed Procession ($59.29) is central to the plan, but Extraplanar Lens ($14.92) and Nykthos ($44.36) are the weaker spends.
Token makers plus Anointed Procession and anthems execute the go-wide half well, but Darien's damage half leans on few real sources and 22 orphan cards dilute the concept (synergy.orphans).

strengths.claim: The land count is exactly at the norm (38 against a 38 target) in a mono-white deck, with 35 white sources against 36 recommended for 80 white pips. Almost no color risk, and the brief marks the high land count with mana-sink lands as deliberate: Kjeldoran Outpost, Faceless Haven and Forbidding Watchtower turn excess lands into Soldiers or creatures.

Sweepers are mostly one-sided for a white Soldier board: Hour of Reckoning spares tokens, Mass Calcify spares white creatures, Martial Coup leaves its new tokens, and Elspeth, Sun's Champion kills only power 4+. Together they reset the table while the plan survives.

Token makers (Hero of Bladehold, Captain of the Watch, Mobilization, Elspeth, Sun's Champion) feed multipliers and payoffs: Anointed Procession doubles every maker, and Myrel makes tokens equal to the Soldier count each attack. Hero's battle cry and Captain's +1/+1 reward the same wide board.

Soldier production is layered across the curve: Precinct Captain and Kjeldoran Outpost early, Mobilization as a mana sink, Hero of Bladehold at 4, Captain of the Watch and Elspeth, Sun's Champion at 6, so a wide board appears in most games. Anointed Procession doubles all of it, and Myrel, Shield of Argive then converts the Soldier count into more tokens each attack.

The main kill is redundant: Hero of Bladehold battle cry, Myrel's token-doubling, Elesh Norn's +2/+2 and -2/-2, Field Marshal, Coat of Arms and True Conviction (double strike and lifelink) all convert a wide Soldier board into lethal in one or two attacks, and the synergy token cluster is commander-centered.

The only rules-based pressure on the bracket is Smothering Tithe, a single Game Changer. There are no complete combos and no tutors, so the deck does not exceed bracket 3 on hard rules and plays as a fair, board-based Soldier deck.

Protection is layered across the commander and the board. Bastion Protector makes Darien indestructible, Flawless Maneuver is free with a commander out, Boromir sacrifices to give indestructible, and Swiftfoot Boots gives hexproof. This covers both a spot removal on Darien and a sweeper on the tokens.

The curve is low for a deck with six-drop commander and seven-drop sweepers. The average MV is 3.45, with 6 one-drops, 13 two-drops and 15 three-drops. Cheap lifegain creatures and cheap makers such as Precinct Captain and Martial Coup mean the board starts early, and Sol Ring and Marble Diamond give a small acceleration floor.

The lifegain-on-entry package (Soul Warden, Soul's Attendant, Healer of the Pride, Suture Priest, Daxos, Anointer Priest) scales with token volume, and Haliya, Guided by Light turns the life into a card at end step. This offsets the painful lands' self-damage and gives the small creatures a clear job, even though the heuristic flags several of them as orphans.

The sweepers are mostly aligned with the plan: Martial Coup, Elspeth, Sun's Champion and Hour of Reckoning (nontoken only) clear the table while leaving tokens. Mass Calcify hits only nonwhite creatures, so the deck can reset without losing its board.

The payoff layer turns the wide board into a kill within a couple of swings. Elesh Norn, Field Marshal, Captain of the Watch and Coat of Arms scale with the Soldier count, while Hero of Bladehold battle cry and True Conviction (double strike, lifelink) multiply the damage. Odric, Master Tactician and Catapult Master add alternate ways to finish.

The deck is protected against its own sweepers and against removal on its engines. Hour of Reckoning, Mass Calcify, Martial Coup and both Elspeths reset the table while leaving white tokens alive. Boromir, Flawless Maneuver, Swiftfoot Boots and Bastion Protector cover Darien and the board.

Cheap exile spot removal (Swords to Plowshares, Path to Exile) lets the deck deal with a lone threat while the board builds. Spear of Heliod and Catapult Master add repeatable answers that scale with the creature count. Myrel also stops opponents from casting spells or activating abilities during the owner's turn.

The deck has real finishing multipliers, not just incremental damage: True Conviction doubles damage across the board, Odric, Master Tactician removes blockers, and Elesh Norn shrinks opposing creatures, so the board is lethal through a stabilizing opponent.

Extraplanar Lens is tagged as removal but works as hidden ramp here. All 24 Snow-Covered Plains share one name, so imprinting one makes every one of them tap for an extra white mana. That eases the 6-7 mana plays (Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite, Captain of the Watch) and the Mobilization sink, which the tagged ramp count of 3 undercounts. The effect depends on actually drawing the Lens.

The two most expensive cards, Anointed Procession and Smothering Tithe, are core to the brief. Anointed Procession doubles every token maker and doubles Darien's damage into Soldiers. Smothering Tithe supplies mana and is the card that sets the bracket 3 floor. The money is concentrated in plan-relevant cards.

Speed indicators are modest. Average MV is 3.45 and the only ramp is Sol Ring, Marble Diamond and Smothering Tithe. The deck wins through Hero of Bladehold, Myrel, Shield of Argive and anthem stacking over several turns rather than a fast burst, which fits an upgraded-table pace.

Most of the engine is cheap. Captain of the Watch, Hero of Bladehold, Mobilization, Martial Coup, Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Glorious Anthem and Hour of Reckoning each cost under $1, so the wide-token core is cheap to rebuild or upgrade. Against a $438.93 total, a handful of cards carry most of the cost.

Backup routes diversify the finish: Halo Fountain's fifteen-creature win needs Mobilization, Captain of the Watch or Anointed Procession tokens, while Catapult Master, Dingus Staff and Suture Priest give incremental reach. These are slow but are independent of combat.

problems.claim: Synergy density is only 0.2333, and 22 cards sit outside any active cluster. Many are single-purpose lifegain pingers (Soul Warden, Soul's Attendant, Auriok Champion, Healer of the Pride, Anointer Priest, Daxos) or overlapping anthems (Glorious Anthem, Dictate of Heliod, Flowering of the White Tree, Pearl Medallion). They add little to the go-wide plan beyond small life gain, and they compete for slots with token makers and draw. The lifegain package is an intentional quirk, but the number of redundant pieces is a real cost.

Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx is $44.36, the third most expensive card. It costs {2} to activate and only pays off with heavy white devotion. The Soldier tokens have no mana cost and add no devotion, so its value depends on a few permanents like Daxos or the enchantments. A cheaper colorless or white mana-sink land would do most of this job in a deck with 38 lands and many sinks.

Darien's trigger depends on a thin set of damage sources. Tarnished Citadel, City of Brass, Nomad Stadium and Grand Coliseum are lands that hurt only when tapped (1 damage each, 3 for Citadel). Blood of the Martyr is a one-shot instant and Jade Monolith needs mana plus an incoming damage source. The result is that Darien makes Soldiers reliably only when opponents attack, and Darien at MV 6 is a weak commander to lean on. Whether this engine is the core plan is unanswered.

Refueling and acceleration are thin for a concept that needs many mana-hungry pieces (Mobilization, Kjeldoran Outpost, Captain of the Watch, Elesh Norn, True Conviction). Draw is 6 against a target of 11, and ramp is 3 against 9. The deck relies on lands for acceleration, and after a sweeper it has few cards to rebuild with. Tutors are 0, so it can't find Anointed Procession or Myrel on demand.

The only answers to enchantments or artifacts are Generous Gift (which hands over a 3/3) and one mode of Austere Command. The deck has no cheap, targeted answer to a stax enchantment or artifact, a graveyard-hate piece against Sun Titan and Emeria, or a hostile planeswalker. The deck itself leans on enchantments (Anointed Procession, Mobilization).

Card flow is thin for a deck that wants to rebuild after wipes: 6 draw pieces against an 11-13 target. Several of them are conditional (Dawn of a New Age, Halo Fountain, Haliya, Guided by Light, Mentor of the Meek), and Smothering Tithe is tagged draw only because opponents draw. Minas Tirith and Windbrisk Heights add some land-based card flow. After Wrath of God or Austere Command the deck relies on topdecks and Skullclamp.

Wrath of God and Austere Command kill the deck's own Soldiers, and Austere Command also hits artifact and enchantment lords. They pull against a go-wide plan when Hour of Reckoning, Mass Calcify, Martial Coup and both Elspeths already cover resets. Recovery relies on Sun Titan, Marshal's Anthem and Skullclamp, which is a small recursion set (roles.recursion.count = 2). This depends on whether they are deliberate safety valves (q-3).

The multiplier and payoff pieces (Anointed Procession, Myrel, Shield of Argive, Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite) are single copies with no tutors (roles.tutors.count = 0) and below-norm draw (roles.draw.count = 6 against a minimum of 11), so the deck cannot reliably find them and often plays as a plain token-and-anthem deck. The deck's own refuel cards (Skullclamp, Mentor of the Meek, Dawn of a New Age, Haliya, Guided by Light) are the only way to dig for them.

The wide-combat plan depends on the board surviving a turn cycle, while the deck has no tutors to find a specific payoff and only two recursion pieces (Marshal's Anthem, Sun Titan). After Wrath of God or Austere Command the rebuild leans on Elspeth, Sun's Champion and Martial Coup, and Darien alone is a slow restart.

Combat is the dominant route to victory. Win paths 3 and 4 are slow: Halo Fountain needs fifteen creatures plus WWWWW and a tap, and Catapult Master needs five untapped Soldiers. Mass removal, fog effects and blockers can stall combat, and Darien's self-damage engine does not itself end the game. Without ramp (roles.ramp.count = 3 against a minimum of 9) the turn the finisher assembles is later than it could be.

The target bracket is unstated (q-1), so the fit cannot be judged. If the owner wants bracket 2, Smothering Tithe is the card forcing the floor to 3 and Anointed Procession, Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite and Sol Ring would also need review. If bracket 3 is the target, nothing is out of range.

Tagged ramp is 3 (Sol Ring, Marble Diamond, Smothering Tithe) against a 9-11 target, and the brief explains the lands as doing the ramp job. The cost remains: the commander Darien is MV 6, and Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Captain of the Watch, True Conviction, Hour of Reckoning and Mass Calcify cluster at 6-7. A light-land draw stalls on those, and Smothering Tithe's Treasure depends on opponents declining to pay.

Colorless-only lands such as Faceless Haven, Scrying Sheets, Reliquary Tower and Nykthos, Shrine to Nyx, plus three unconditional tapped lands, sit alongside 80 white pips. The 35 white sources are one short of the 36 recommended. Faceless Haven and Scrying Sheets also need snow mana, which Snow-Covered Plains supply. The impact is small but real on turns 2-3 when you need W or WW for Precinct Captain, Mobilization and Anointer Priest.

Many payoffs are generic rather than Soldier- or token-specific. Glorious Anthem, Dictate of Heliod, Coat of Arms, Flowering of the White Tree and Pearl Medallion are stat boosts or cost reducers, and Dingus Staff and Eldrazi Monument sit apart from the token engine, so the plan is more a pile of anthems than a tight engine. The synergy density is low (synergy.density = 0.2333).

Wrath of God and Austere Command are full sweepers that kill the deck's own Soldiers, unlike the five token-friendly effects. Recovery after them relies on Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Sun Titan, Marshal's Anthem and Skullclamp. Whether they are deliberate safety valves is unknown, so this is a cost to weigh rather than a defect.

Coat of Arms is $17.68 and in a Soldier deck it behaves like a strong anthem. It also pumps opponents' creatures that share types, and several Soldier-adjacent anthems already exist (Glorious Anthem, Marshal's Anthem, Spear of Heliod, Intangible Virtue). It is a candidate for a cheaper anthem slot if cost matters.

Wrath of God and Austere Command kill the deck's own Soldiers, unlike the token-friendly sweepers. If they are not deliberate safety valves they undercut the concept, and recovery then relies on Sun Titan or Marshal's Anthem with only 2 recursion pieces.

Resilience to losing engine pieces is limited. Anointed Procession, a single enchantment, doubles every token maker, and the deck has no tutors (roles.tutors.count) to find replacements. Protection is mostly aimed at creatures and Darien, with only Flawless Maneuver and Boromir covering the board, and Swiftfoot Boots protects one creature at a time.

If the owner targets a higher bracket (q-1), the deck is light on acceleration and consistency: ramp is 3 against a 9-11 target range, there are zero tutors, and no combos. Halo Fountain's fifteen-creature win is the only alternate finish. Land count may compensate for ramp; that depends on the target.

The closing turn is gated by a few expensive pieces: Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite (MV 7), True Conviction, Captain of the Watch and Elspeth, Sun's Champion (MV 6 each). Only three ramp pieces (Marble Diamond, Smothering Tithe, Sol Ring) are in the list, so these arrive on turns 6-7 by land drops alone unless Sol Ring is drawn early. The owner chose a land-heavy, low-ramp build, and Pearl Medallion plus the low average MV of 3.45 give a cheap early token base. The cost is that the finishing anthem or double-strike turn comes later than the cheap token engine suggests, which gives opponents time to sweep or stabilize.

top_changes.why_these_first: Swaps 1 and 2 go after the deck's thinnest axis, card flow: 6 draw pieces against an 11-13 target (p-mana_consistency-1, p-concept_execution-3). Belladonna Took and Tocasia's Welcome both draw off Soldier tokens that Hero of Bladehold, Mobilization and Anointed Procession already produce in bulk, and extra draw also helps find single-copy engines like Anointed Procession and Myrel with no tutors. The cost is real. Flowering of the White Tree is a cheap 2-mana +1/+1 for nonlegendary creatures that also gives legendary creatures like Darien +2/+1 and ward, and Dictate of Heliod is a flash +2/+2 that can ambush-pump the whole team and beat damage-based sweepers in combat. Both are better than their EDHREC rates suggest. But Glorious Anthem, Marshal's Anthem, Coat of Arms and Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite already make the wide board lethal in one or two swings (s-win_paths_closing-1), and the synergy report flags both as orphans, so the lost stats are the cheapest thing to give up. Swap 3 puts Return to Dust in for Austere Command. It adds the deck's first cheap answer to a stax enchantment or artifact (p-interaction_resilience-2), since Generous Gift hands the opponent a 3/3. It also drops a wipe that kills your own Soldiers, leaving the count at 5, inside the 5-7 target. Swap 4 (Heraldic Banner for Pearl Medallion) trades cost reduction for a slower rock, so it can wait.

swaps.tradeoff: Flowering of the White Tree is a +1/+1 anthem for nonlegendary creatures, so cutting it removes a bit of board stat, though Glorious Anthem, Marshal's Anthem and others still cover that job. Belladonna Took gains life on the first token each turn, draws on the second, and adds counters on the third, so it turns mass token entry into the card flow the deck lacks after sweepers. It is a 2-mana legendary body that dies easily.

Dictate of Heliod is a 5-mana +2/+2 anthem with flash, and cutting it removes a big stat boost that the rest of the anthem pile partly duplicates (Glorious Anthem, Elesh Norn, Coat of Arms). Tocasia's Welcome is a 3-mana enchantment that draws once a turn when a creature with mana value 3 or less enters, and every Soldier token qualifies. It only triggers once per turn and does nothing on its own with an empty board.

Austere Command is a 6-mana sorcery that kills your own Soldiers in most modes, so cutting it also drops a full reset. That leaves the wipe count at 5, within the 5-7 target, and the token-friendly resets are untouched. Return to Dust is an instant that exiles one or two artifacts or enchantments, answering stax pieces cheaply, but it does nothing against creatures or planeswalkers.
swaps.budget_effect: price of the add is unavailable; ownership unknown

swaps.tradeoff: Pearl Medallion costs only 2 and makes every white spell cheaper, including the 6-7 mana top end, so cutting it gives up that cost reduction and costs $9.56 of value. Heraldic Banner costs 3 but taps for white and gives your white Soldiers +1/+0, adding real ramp and a small combat bonus. Casting it a turn later is the price.

cuts_to_consider.reason: It forces a creature sacrifice every upkeep or the Monument itself is sacrificed, and it sits outside the token engine. Only about 13% of decks play it, so the flying and indestructible is better spent on Unbreakable Formation-style one-shot protection or more makers.
It only fires if an opponent has more lands than you, which is unlikely with 38 lands in the deck, and it is an orphan in the synergy data. The slot would do more as a token maker or a draw spell.

questions_for_owner.question: What bracket or power level is this deck meant to play at?
questions_for_owner.why_asked: The minimum is bracket 3 from Smothering Tithe. If bracket 3 is the target, Anointed Procession, Smothering Tithe and Elesh Norn, Grand Cenobite are in range. If a lower table is intended, Smothering Tithe is the problem card to review. If higher, the lack of tutors (none) and combos becomes a gap.

questions_for_owner.question: Is Darien's self-damage engine (painful lands, Blood of the Martyr, Jade Monolith) the core plan, or is the deck mainly a Soldier-anthem and lifegain deck where Darien is just the commander?
questions_for_owner.why_asked: If the damage engine is core, reviewers should judge it on how reliably it makes Soldiers and push for more redirection or pinger effects. If it is incidental, the painful lands and redirection cards may be judged as cost without payoff and the lifegain package becomes the focus.

questions_for_owner.question: Are Wrath of God and Austere Command deliberate full resets, or leftovers next to the token-friendly sweepers?
questions_for_owner.why_asked: If they are deliberate safety valves, they are kept and judged on whether the deck can rebuild after them (Elspeth, Sun's Champion, Sun Titan, Marshal's Anthem, Skullclamp). If not, they may be swapped for sweepers that spare tokens.
